name: Minimum coprime integer-square dissection of a 1000 square
definition: Partition a 1000 by 1000 square into the fewest axis-aligned squares with positive integer side lengths whose greatest common divisor is 1.
solution_format: An object with squares, a list of [x,y,side] integer triples describing each square's lower-left corner and side length.
constraints: Each tile is an axis-aligned square with positive integer side length less than 1000.
All tile coordinates and side lengths are integers.
The tiles cover the entire outer square.
The greatest common divisor of all tile side lengths is 1.
Compound or sub-quilt arrangements are allowed.
verification: The checker validates integer squares and bounds, requires gcd 1, and uses one exact bit mask per integer x-column to reject overlap and prove that every cell of the 1000 by 1000 square is covered.
